translation:
Sanhuang Wan (三黃丸) chiefly treats the five fatigues and seven injuries of men and women, wasting-thirst with failure to generate flesh and muscle, and also women's vaginal discharge (帶下) with cold and heat arising in the hands and feet. (This formula is found in the nineteenth volume of the Qianjin Yifang (千金翼方); the dosages differ slightly.)

(The Chishui Xuanzhu (赤水玄珠), volume three, "Kouwen" (口問), records this formula, saying: it chiefly treats excess heat of the triple burner. The dosages are all the same as here, except that in the summer months Coptis is made five liang.)

Spring months: Scutellaria (黃芩) (four liang), rhubarb (大黃) (two liang; the Yi (翼) makes it three liang), Coptis (黃連) (four liang).

Summer months: Scutellaria (six liang), rhubarb (one liang), Coptis (one liang; the Yi makes it seven liang).

Autumn months: Scutellaria (six liang), rhubarb (two liang), Coptis (two liang; the Ji (冀) makes it three liang).

Winter months: Scutellaria (three liang), rhubarb (five liang), Coptis (two liang).

Grind the above three ingredients, adjusting the amounts according to the season, into a fine powder, refine honey into pills the size of soybeans; take five pills each time, three times daily. If it does not resolve, add seven pills.
translator_notes: 《翼》/《冀》 both refer to the Qianjin Yifang; 冀 appears to be a typo for 翼.
